entities.summary: Giovanni Battista Caporali was a prominent Italian painter of the High Renaissance, active in Florence during the late 16th century. Born in the 1520s to a family of modest means, Caporali's artistic talent was recognized early, and he apprenticed with the renowned painter Domenico Ghirlandaio. He eventually established his own workshop, creating altarpieces and devotional paintings that showcased his mastery of sfumato and chiaroscuro. Caporali's most famous work, the 'Assumption of the Virgin,' is now housed in the Uffizi Gallery in Florence, a testament to his skill and artistry. Through his paintings, Caporali contributed to the evolution of the Renaissance style, influencing generations of artists to come. His legacy can be seen in the works of artists such as Titian and Caravaggio, who built upon his techniques and innovations. The 'Assumption of the Virgin' remains a landmark of Caporali's oeuvre, a masterpiece that continues to captivate art lovers and scholars alike.
